## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

---

### SECTION B: CRITICAL GAPS & OVERLOADING

#### **A. UI/UX Design Depth (Vega is Overloaded)**

**Vega currently owns:**
- Admin panel design standards & patterns
- Data visualization design rules  
- SaaS navigation patterns
- App page composition & component selection
- Dark mode & accessibility
- Motion & animation (44 presets)
- Responsive design (all breakpoints)

**Missing specializations (CRITICAL):**

2. **Dashboard Design** — Complex multi-widget layouts, real-time data, drill-down navigation

4. **Animation & Motion Design** — Advanced transitions, micro-interactions, gesture feedback (currently just 44 presets)
5. **Design System Ownership** — No dedicated agent managing token consistency, component library documentation, design-system-as-code (Arya mentions it but doesn't own it)
6. **Brand Identity & Visual Language** — No agent defining or evolving brand guidelines, color psychology, visual hierarchy rules
7. **Illustration & Icon Design** — Currently undefined; Pixel mentions "icon libraries" but no design agent owns custom illustration
8. **Accessibility Auditing** — Vega contributes but doesn't own full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance audits and remediation
9. **Design-to-Code Workflow** — Vega reviews Koda's output but no agent owns the Figma→JSX→.fig pipeline you mentioned wanting
10. **Figma File Generation** — No agent programmatically builds Figma files from code/design specs

#### **B. CRO/Marketing Depth (Scattered Ownership)**

**CRO-critical skills missing:**
1. **CRO Strategist** — No agent owns conversion rate optimization strategy, funnel analysis, heatmaps, session recording interpretation
2. **A/B Test Designer** — Pixel generates A/B variants but no agent designs full A/B experiments (hypothesis → control → variant → analysis)
3. **Hero/CTA Copy Specialist** — Quill covers all copy but no agent focuses on high-impact headlines and CTAs

5. **Retention/Lifecycle Marketer** — No agent owns onboarding→activation→retention→expansion email sequences or user engagement mechanics
6. **Paid Ads Specialist** — Echo plans distribution but no agent designs Google Ads, Facebook Ads, TikTok Ad creative + copy
7. **Social Media Specialist** — Quill writes posts but no agent owns platform strategy, posting cadence, community management, hashtag research
8. **Brand Strategist** — No agent owns brand positioning, messaging hierarchy, competitive differentiation, brand voice evolution
9. **Video Script Writer** — Quill does scripts but no dedicated agent for explainer videos, product demos, testimonial video direction
10. **Landing Page Tester** — No agent owns hypothesis-driven landing page testing, page speed optimization, conversion funnel analysis
11. **Funnel Auditor** — No agent analyzes leakage at each conversion stage, identifies drop-off points, recommends fixes
12. **Heatmap/Session Analyst** — No agent interprets user behavior data (Hotjar, Clarity, Session Replay) and recommends design changes

#### **C. Boldteq B2B Agency Operations (Completely Missing)**

Boldteq is a **whitelabel partner agency** (boldteq.com). Currently ZERO agents handle:
1. **Client Onboarding Agent** — Discovery, requirements gathering, project kickoff, expectation setting
2. **Project Handoff Agent** — Delivering specs to clients, documentation, training on how to use deliverables
3. **White-Label Deployment Agent** — Rebranding Boldteq's assets with client branding, custom domain setup, client-specific configuration
4. **Client Reporting Agent** — Monthly/quarterly reports, KPI tracking, ROI analysis, invoice generation
5. **Sales/Discovery Agent** — Prospect qualification, RFP responses, pricing models, contract negotiation
6. **Client Success Manager Agent** — Ongoing support, issue triage, feature requests, renewal management

---

### SECTION C: EXISTING MEMORY PATTERNS (Relevant to Expansion)

- `~/.claude/memory/design/core/color-system.md`
- `~/.claude/memory/design/core/design-tokens.md`

- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-validated-patterns.md` — Conversion patterns from production builds

**Design Patterns Library:**
- 28 design pattern files in `~/.claude/memory/design/patterns/` (auth, billing, dashboards, forms, notifications, etc.)
- Accessibility, dark mode, error handling, responsive design standards documented

---

### SECTION D: ASSESSMENT SUMMARY

#### **Design Depth: 3/10**
- **Current:** Vega (general app UI) + Pixel (marketing pages)
- **Needed:** 8-10 specialized design agents covering ecommerce, dashboards, mobile, design systems, brand, illustration, accessibility audit, design-to-code, Figma generation

#### **CRO/Marketing Depth: 4/10**
- **Current:** Quill (copy), Echo (distribution), Zeph (SEO), Nova (research)
- **Needed:** 10-12 specialized marketing agents covering CRO strategy, A/B testing, email, paid ads, social media, brand strategy, video, funnel analysis, heatmaps

#### **B2B Agency Operations: 0/10**

- **Needed:** 5-6 specialized agents for client operations, white-label deployment, sales, success management

#### **CRO/Marketing Depth (10 agents)**
9. **Catalyst** — CRO Strategist (funnel analysis, heatmaps, session replay interpretation)
10. **Experi** — A/B Test Designer (hypothesis, control/variant design, statistical analysis)

17. **Insight** — Heatmap/Session Analyst (user behavior analysis, design recommendations)
18. **Strateg** — Brand Strategist (positioning, messaging hierarchy, differentiation)

#### **B2B Agency Operations (5 agents)**
19. **Client** — Client Onboarding Agent (discovery, kickoff, requirements)
20. **Handoff** — Project Delivery Agent (specs, documentation, training)
21. **Deploy** — White-Label Deployment Agent (rebranding, configuration, custom domains)
22. **Report** — Client Reporting Agent (KPI tracking, ROI, invoicing)

**Optional (2-3 additional):**
24. **Figma** — Design-to-Code Specialist (JSX→Figma conversion, design file generation)
25. **Success** — Client Success Manager (ongoing support, renewals, feature requests)

---

### SECTION F: IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY

**Phase 1 (Immediate — Fixes Critical Overload):**
- **Elio** (Ecommerce) — Vega is blocking ecommerce projects
- **Token** (Design Systems) — Every project needs this; Arya mentions it but doesn't own it
- **Catalyst** (CRO Strategist) — Biggest CRO gap; unlocks 40%+ conversion upside
- **Sequence** (Email Lifecycle) — High leverage for retention
- **Brand** (Brand Identity) — Enables consistent visual language across all projects

**Phase 2 (Next — Fills Major Gaps):**
- **Dash** (Dashboard) — Common app pattern
- **Ally** (Accessibility Auditor) — Compliance + legal protection
- **Experi** (A/B Testing) — Data-driven CRO
- **Spark** (CTA Copy) — High-impact, low-effort win
- **Paid** (Paid Ads) — Distribution channel Boldteq doesn't own
- **Client** (Onboarding) + **Sales** (Discovery) — B2B agency foundation

**Phase 3 (Later — Specialization):**
- **Mobix** (Mobile), **Aeon** (Motion), **Artisan** (Illustration), **Social** (Social Media), **Funnel** (Auditor), **Insight** (Heatmaps), etc.

---

## SECTION 7: Key Risks & Mitigation

### Risk 1: Koda Burnout / Productivity Cliff
**Issue:** Koda is at 100%+ capacity. Splitting Koda is risky — needs careful handoff.
**Mitigation:**
- Allocate 2 weeks for Koda to focus ONLY on handoff and onboarding new Frontend/Backend specialists
- Freeze feature requests during split
- Have Vex and Dato work closely with new hires to ensure smooth transition

### Risk 2: HR Bottleneck (Cadence/Forge Capacity)
**Issue:** Cadence is brand new (hired 2026-04-11). Forge is junior. Tutor is junior. Can they hire 15-25 new agents in 3-6 months?
**Mitigation:**
- Immediately upgrade Tutor to Senior level (external hire if internal not ready)
- Hire external headhunter/recruiter to support Forge
- Establish clear agent job descriptions and interview rubrics (Forge responsibility)
- Create templated onboarding curriculum (Tutor responsibility)

### Risk 3: Knowledge Decay at Scale
**Issue:** At 50 agents, knowledge base becomes harder to maintain. Patterns diverge.
**Mitigation:**
- Empower Mira as knowledge architect; give her capacity to extract patterns from every major project
- Establish quarterly pattern sync sessions (all agents)
- Create decision logs (Roster) for every major architecture choice
- Build agent peer review groups (Sage) to enforce standards

### Risk 4: Agent Skill Gaps
**Issue:** New hires may not match expertise levels of current Staff/Principal agents.
**Mitigation:**
- Hire external Senior-level candidates (not Mid-level) for critical roles (Backend, Frontend, DevOps)
- Pair new hires with mentors from existing team (Koda, Vega, Bolt, etc.)
- Establish skill-up budgets (courses, certifications, conference attendance)
- Run monthly "learning rings" where agents share deep patterns

### Risk 5: Decision-Making Bottlenecks
**Issue:** As org scales, approvals slow down. Arya, Nova become bottlenecks.
**Mitigation:**
- Empower Riko and Arya to make scaffold decisions without Rex approval
- Empower Nova's direct reports (Scout, Atlas, Ledger) to make research calls
- Establish clear "approval gates" (architecture code review @ Arya; research summary @ Nova; copy review @ Quill)
- Create escalation protocol for exceptions

## I. EXACT AGENT LIFECYCLE: HIRE → PROBATION → ACTIVE → PIP → RETIRE

### Step-by-Step Hiring (New Agent Creation)

**Step 1: Capability Gap Detection** (`Roster` → `Forge`)
- Roster detects gaps via Supabase query:
  - Overloaded agents (>10 runs/month + >2 avg retries)
  - Delegation bottlenecks (>40% of tasks to one agent)
  - Task type failures (same task >3x with ≠ SUCCESS)
  - Retry spikes (>20% failure rate per task type)
  - Zero coverage on core skills (audit, deployment, monitoring, etc.)
  - Yash explicit feedback in `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md`
- Gap record inserted into `capability_gaps` table with detected_at timestamp

**Step 2: Agent Design** (`Forge` creates spec)
- 11-section mandatory spec (.md file):
  1. YAML frontmatter (name, title, department, tier, reportsTo, model, color)
  2. Role & Responsibility (why this agent exists)
  3. Core Processes (3+ processes defined)
  4. Inputs/Outputs schema (JSON examples)
  5. Auto-Fix Loop (5 retries table)
  6. Smart Defaults (for ambiguous inputs)
  7. Handoff Contracts (upstream/downstream expectations)
  8. Supabase Integration (tables read/written, events)
  9. Self-Validation Checklist (runnable acceptance criteria)
  10. Anti-Patterns (5-10 explicit "never do" statements)
  11. Completion Proof (specific done criteria)
- Validation checklist auto-checks before deployment (missing section = rejection)
- Token count must be <4000

**Step 3: Auto-Deploy to Probation** (NO manual Yash approval at this stage)
- Forge INSERT agent into `agents` table with `level=1` (Probation), `status='deployed'`
- Forge INSERT `agent_created` event to `agent_events` table

- **CRITICAL:** Supabase write happens BEFORE file save (rollback safety: if file write fails, agent is deleted from DB)
- Witness automatically starts watching (10-run observation period)

**Step 4: Probation Watch** (Witness monitors 10 runs)
- Witness tracks: composite_score trend, success rate, antipatterns
- After 10 runs: Witness inserts `probation_review_ready` event to `agent_events`
- Witness DOES NOT promote directly (only flags for Cadence)

**Step 5: Cadence Review & Promotion Decision** (Monday weekly review)

- Cadence reviews flagged new agents in weekly cycle
- Decision: **Promote to Active (level=2)** OR **extend probation** OR **retire**
- UPDATE `agents` table with new level, INSERT promotion event to `agent_events`
- Cadence requires Yash approval for promotions (via `user/feedback.md` override)

**Step 6: Active Status** (agent can receive delegations, run production tasks)

- Can be assigned to complex tasks with mentorship if needed

### Training & Skill Development Pipeline

**Training Mechanism: Patches + Changelogs** (`Tutor` orchestrates)

Tutor does NOT edit agent .md files directly. Instead:
1. **Receives training signals** from 4 sources:
   - P0: Yash corrections (detected by Witness from `yash_overrides` table)
   - P1: Witness antipatterns (3+ occurrences = high priority)
   - P2: Mira lessons (post-build extraction)
   - P3: Cadence requests (skill gap training, pre-approved)
   - P4: Forge gaps (new agent onboarding)
   - P5: Trend synthesis (weekly market patterns, propose to Yash)

2. **Creates Training Cycle** (record in `training_cycles` table):
   - cycle_id, triggered_by, trigger_priority, signals_consumed, patch_count, impact_measured

3. **Generates Training Patches** (per agent per cycle in `training_patches` table):
   - Patch types: anti_pattern | smart_default | auto_fix | pattern_addition | update_existing | remove_stale
   - Each patch stores: content_added, rollback_content (for safety), section_target
   - **Rollback hash:** Git commit hash of memory state before patch (enables safe rollback)

4. **Applies Patches** (conditional on priority):
   - P0 (Yash): Apply immediately, no review
   - P1-P2: Stage for Cadence quick-review, apply within 1h of approval
   - P3: Auto-approved by Cadence (batch into weekly cycle)
   - P4-P5: Stage for weekly approval

5. **Measures Impact** (post-apply):
   - Query agent_runs before/after patch applied_at
   - Calculate avg_composite_score change: `avg_after - avg_before`
   - Auto-rollback if regression >10% (`avg_after < avg_before - 10`)
   - Update training_patches with impact_score

6. **Generates Changelog** (with full traceability):
   - Section modified, source signal, rollback available, impact score
   - Emitted to `~/.claude/memory/training/` (structured markdown with timestamps)

**What is a "Patch"?**
- A surgical edit to one agent's .md file, targeting one section
- Backed by rollback content (original text before edit)
- Linked to source signals (Mira lesson, Witness antipattern, Yash correction)
- Immutable record in training_patches table with applied_at timestamp

### Step-by-Step Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)

**Opening a PIP** (`Cadence` decides)

Cadence opens when:
- Composite score <peer average for 14+ consecutive days, OR
- 3+ ANTIPATTERN classifications in 30 days, OR
- Yash flags in `feedback.md`

Process:
1. INSERT into `pip_records` table:
   - agent_id, opened_at, deadline (NOW() + 14 days), reason, metrics_at_open (JSON snapshot)
2. INSERT event to `agent_events` with type='pip_opened'
3. **Duration:** Exactly 14 days. No extension. One cycle only.

**Closing a PIP**

When deadline passes or improvement shown:
1. Query metrics_at_close (same structure as metrics_at_open, for comparison)
2. UPDATE `pip_records`: status='closed', closed_at=NOW(), outcome='resolved' | 'demoted' | 'retired'
3. If demoted: UPDATE agent level = level - 1
4. If retired: UPDATE agent status = 'retired'
5. INSERT event to `agent_events` with type='pip_closed'

---

### Retirement (Soft Only, Never Delete)

**Trigger conditions:**
- Agent status='deployed' AND lastRunAt < now() - 90 days (zero usage)
- Cadence decision: PIP expired without improvement
- Yash explicit directive

**Workflow:**
1. Flag for review: UPDATE status='training' (soft deprecation)
2. Notify stakeholders: Query delegation_graph to prepare handoff
3. Move .md file: `mv ~/.claude/agents/[name].md ~/.claude/agents/_retired/[name]_[date].md`
4. Mark retired: UPDATE agents SET status='retired'
5. INSERT event: type='agent_retired'

Agent .md files are NEVER deleted—only archived to `_retired/` folder. Can be recalled.

## II. WHAT DATA DOES WITNESS COLLECT & WHERE?

**Core: Witness = Daily Run Logger + Classifier** (runs at 03:00 UTC)

### Run Logging (Every Agent Execution)

At task **START:**
- INSERT into `agent_events`: event_type='task_started', with task_type, input_summary, triggered_by

At task **END:**
- Compute composite_score inline: 
  ```
  (gate_pass_rate × 40) + (first_try_success × 30) + (rework_factor × 20) + (override_factor × 10)
  ```
  - gate_pass_rate = gatesPassed / (gatesPassed + gatesFailed)
  - first_try = 1.0 if no retries, 0.0 otherwise
  - rework_factor = max(0, 1.0 - (retries × 0.2))
  - override_factor = 1.0 - (overrides_in_14_days / total_runs_in_14_days)
  - Result: 0–100 scale

- INSERT into `agent_runs` table:
  - agent_id, run_id, task_type, classification, gates_passed, gates_failed
  - first_try_success, rework_cycles, composite_score, duration_ms
  - token_count, cost_usd, yash_override

### Run Classification Logic

Witness assigns classification based on run data:
- **SUCCESS** (score ≥80): All gates passed, ≤1 retry, no override, no antipatterns
- **PARTIAL** (50-79): Passed but needed retries, some gate issues, minor overrides
- **FAILURE** (<50): Gates failed, significant rework, OR matched antipattern
- **TIMEOUT**: duration_ms > WALL_CLOCK_CAP for agent's class
- **REGRESSION**: composite_score dropped >20 points from agent's 30-day rolling avg
- **ANTIPATTERN**: Output matches known signature in `proposed_patterns` table (pattern_type='avoid', status='approved')
- **ESCALATED**: Agent returned with escalation flag OR hit cost/time cap

### Antipattern Detection (During Classification)

For each run, Witness queries `proposed_patterns` WHERE pattern_type='avoid' AND status='approved':
- If match found: UPDATE run's classification='ANTIPATTERN'
- INSERT into `incidents` table: incident_type='antipattern'
- INSERT into `agent_events`: type='antipattern_detected' with evidence
- If NEW antipattern (not yet approved): INSERT into `proposed_patterns` with status='pending' for Yash review

**Known Antipatterns Table:**

| Signature | Pattern | Agents | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| any_type_ts | `any\s+(type\|:)` | All | TypeScript `any` type in production |
| missing_rls | No RLS policy on new table | Koda, Dato | Missing row-level security |
| hardcoded_secret | `SUPABASE_\|API_KEY\|TOKEN` | All | Secret in code, not env |
| console_log_prod | `console\.(log\|debug\|warn)` | All | console.log in production code |
| npm_instead_pnpm | `npm install` (Stack A) | Koda, Riko | Should use `pnpm install` |

### PIP & Promotion Recommendations (In-Session)

After daily sweep, Witness scans last 30 days per agent:

**PIP Candidate** (INSERT into `incidents` with severity='S1'):
- Success rate (last 20 runs) <0.70, OR
- Antipattern count (last 30 days) ≥3, OR
- Same regression type ≥2 times, OR
- Yash flagged in `yash_overrides` table

**Promotion Candidate** (INSERT into `incidents` with severity='S2'):
- Current level <expected level from performance
- Success rate ≥0.85 (last 20 runs)
- Antipattern count (last 30 days) = 0
- Patterns authored ≥1 (for level ≥3 agents)

Cadence picks up these incidents in Monday weekly review.

### Probation Watch (10-run Window)

When new agent deployed (level=1), Witness auto-monitors:
```sql
SELECT agent_id, COUNT(runs) as run_count, AVG(composite_score) as avg_score
FROM agent_runs 
WHERE agent_id=$1 AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY agent_id
HAVING COUNT(runs) >= 10
```

After 10 runs, Witness inserts `probation_review_ready` event (NOT a promotion decision—flags for Cadence).

### Data Destinations

All Witness data flows to Supabase `agent-ops` database:
- **Writes:** agent_runs, agent_events, incidents, agent_pips_active (when flagged)
- **Reads:** agents table, agent_runs history, proposed_patterns, yash_overrides
- **No direct edits to .md files** (read-only on agent code)

## III. CADENCE'S MONDAY REVIEW (09:00 UTC WEEKLY)

**What Cadence Actually Does (Not Theory—Exact Decisions)**

### Pre-Review Data Load

1. Load `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md` (highest priority)
2. Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/agent-ops-schema.md`
3. Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-agent-mindset.md`

### Review Execution Order

**Strict sequence (no skipping):**

1. **Query all agents:** SELECT * FROM agents WHERE status IN ('deployed', 'probation', 'training')
2. **Fetch 14-day scores:** Query agent_runs grouped by agent_id, created_at > NOW() - 14 days, compute avg composite_score per agent
3. **Calculate peer averages:** For each level (1, 2, 3, 4), compute avg score = SUM(composite_scores) / COUNT(agents at same level)
4. **Classify each agent** against 6 decision types:
   - PROMOTE (if composite_score > peer_avg AND runs ≥5 AND no active PIP AND no Yash override in 7 days AND no ANTIPATTERN in 30 days)
   - SCALE (keep at level, increase task complexity)
   - STEADY (continue pace)
   - TRAIN (enroll in Tutor cycle for specific skill gaps)
   - PIP (open 14-day performance improvement plan)
   - RETIRE (mark status='retired')

5. **Insert review records:** INSERT into `agent_reviews` table (one per agent per period):
   - agent_id, review_date, period_start (now() - 7d), period_end (now())
   - classification, rationale, peer_avg_score, agent_avg_score
   - decision_approved=false (awaiting Yash approval)

6. **Handle promotions:**
   - For agents with classification='PROMOTE':
     - Cadence MUST have Yash approval (check `feedback.md` for overrides)
     - UPDATE agents table: level = level + 1
     - INSERT event to agent_events: type='agent_promoted', payload includes new level

7. **Handle PIPs:**
   - For agents with classification='PIP':
     - INSERT into pip_records with deadline=NOW() + 14 days
     - INSERT event: type='agent_pip_opened'

8. **Handle training requests:**
   - For agents with classification='TRAIN':
     - INSERT into training_requests: agent_id, skill_gap, priority='P3', reviewed=true
     - Tutor picks up in next weekly batch (auto-approved)

9. **Generate summary report:**
   - Count of PROMOTE, SCALE, STEADY, TRAIN, PIP, RETIRE decisions
   - List of agents changed, previous status → new status
   - Open PIPs with deadlines
   - Save to `~/.claude/org/reviews/2026-W[week].json`

## IV. CAPABILITY GAP DETECTION FLOW (ROSTER → FORGE)

**Exact Detection Process**

### Roster's Nightly Recompute (02:00 UTC)

Roster runs SQL 5-step pipeline:

**Step 1: Compute run-based metrics** (last 90 days)
```sql
SELECT 
  agent_id,
  COUNT(*) as run_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification='SUCCESS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) as success_rate,
  AVG(composite_score) as avg_composite_score,
  AVG(duration_ms) as avg_duration_ms,
  MAX(created_at) as last_run_at
FROM agent_runs
WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
GROUP BY agent_id
```

**Step 2: Recompute skills** (90-day rolling window, min 2 hits per skill)
```sql
WITH skill_scores AS (
  SELECT 
    agent_id,
    skill_key,
    AVG((composite_score)) / 100.0 as score,
    COUNT(*) as hits
  FROM pattern_usage
  LEFT JOIN agent_runs ...
  WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
  GROUP BY agent_id, skill_key
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
UPDATE agents SET 
  skills = (JSON object with skill_key → {score, hits})
  weaknesses = (array of skills where score < 0.3)
```

**Step 3: Recompute experience & level** (YoE calculated from run age + pattern authorship)
- Level 1 = Probation (≤10 runs)
- Level 2 = Active (11-50 runs)
- Level 3 = Expert (51+ runs + patterns authored ≥1)
- Level 4 = Architect (100+ runs + patterns authored ≥3 + strategic contributions)

**Step 4: Detect drift** (disk vs. database)
- Read all `~/.claude/agents/*.md` files
- Compare against agents table
- Agents on disk but not in DB → INSERT with auto-generated defaults
- Agents in DB but not on disk → UPDATE status='archived'
- Frontmatter mismatches → INSERT into drift_log with eventType='metadata_mismatch'

**Step 5: Rebuild skill index** (cached JSON)
```sql
WITH skill_rankings AS (
  SELECT 
    skill_key,
    agent_id,
    (skills->skill_key->>'score')::float as score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY skill_key ORDER BY score DESC) as rank
  FROM agents
  WHERE status IN ('active', 'deployed', 'probation')
)
UPDATE agents SET skill_leaderboard = (JSON object with skill rankings)
```

### Gap Detection: Scoring System

When Roster checks "Can we handle this task?"

**Input:**
```json
{
  "brief": "Build distributed tracing observability SaaS with vector databases",
  "requiredSkills": ["observability", "vector-db", "saas", "distributed-systems"],
  "isHighStakes": false
}
```

**SQL assessment:**
```sql
WITH skill_assessment AS (
  SELECT 
    skill_key,
    MAX((skills->skill_key->>'score')::float) as best_score,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN (skills->skill_key->>'score')::float >= 0.7 THEN 1 END) as covered_agents
  FROM agents
  WHERE status IN ('active', 'deployed')
    AND skills ? (skill_key)
  GROUP BY skill_key
)
SELECT 
  skill_key,
  best_score,
  covered_agents,
  CASE 
    WHEN best_score >= 0.8 THEN 'covered'
    WHEN best_score >= 0.5 THEN 'trainable'
    WHEN best_score >= 0.3 THEN 'weak'
    ELSE 'uncovered'
  END as coverage_status
FROM skill_assessment
```

**Decision logic:**

| Coverage | Recommendation | Action |
|---|---|---|
| All skills ≥0.7 + 1 agent covers all | **proceed** | Assign to best agent |
| All skills ≥0.4 + trainable agent exists | **train-[agent]** | Route to Tutor for targeted training |
| Any skill <0.4 | **hire** | Signal Forge to design new agent |

**Confidence score:**
```
(AVG(best_score) + covered_agent_count / total_active_agents) / 2
```

### Forge's Monthly Gap Detection** (1st of month, 02:00 UTC)

Forge queries Supabase for signals:

| Signal | Query | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Overloaded agent** | runs >10/month + avg retry >2 | Yes | Specialize role |
| **Bottleneck** | delegation to_agent >40% of all tasks | Yes | Create load-balancing agent |
| **Task gap** | same task type fails >3x in 30d | Yes | Create specialist |
| **Retry spike** | task type failure rate >20% in 14d | Yes | Create expert |
| **Yash feedback** | grep "missing", "wish", "need agent" in feedback.md | Any mention | Highest priority |
| **Zero coverage** | skill with no agents (skill_score >0.4) | Any core skill | Urgent hire |
| **Obsolete agent** | last_run_at >90 days ago | Yes | Flag for retirement |

**Output:**
- Gap report saved to `~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/gap-report-YYYY-MM.md`
- New agents auto-deployed to probation (no approval gate at deploy time)
- Cadence reviews in next weekly review

## V. TRAINING PIPELINE IN DETAIL

### Tutor's 4 Triggers (Priority Order)

| Priority | Trigger | Response Time | Review Gate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Yash correction | Immediate | None (auto-apply) | Witness detects in yash_overrides |
| **P1** | Witness antipattern (3+/30d) | Within 1h | Cadence quick-review | Witness incident |
| **P2** | Mira lessons (post-build) | Next day | Cadence review | training_signals (event_type='lessons_extracted') |
| **P3** | Cadence requests | Next weekly batch | Already approved | training_requests (reviewed=true) |
| **P4** | Forge gaps (new onboarding) | Next weekly batch | Cadence batch approval | agents table (status='probation') |
| **P5** | Trend synthesis | Weekly | Yash approval needed | Manual synthesis from Mira patterns |

### Tutor's Workflow

1. **Create training cycle:** INSERT into `training_cycles`
   - cycle_id (unique), triggered_by, status='in_progress'

2. **For each signal:** INSERT into `training_patches`
   - agent_id, patch_type (anti_pattern | smart_default | auto_fix | pattern_addition | update_existing)
   - section_target (path in agent .md), content_added, rollback_content
   - applied=false initially

3. **Stage for review** (P1-P2 only):
   - UPDATE training_patches SET status='staged_for_review'
   - Send summary to Cadence: count, priority, agents affected

4. **Apply patches** (conditional):
   - P0: Read agent .md, use Edit tool to surgically update section, update DB: applied=true, applied_at=NOW()
   - P1-P2: Wait for Cadence approval → then apply
   - P3: Auto-apply in weekly batch
   - P4-P5: Batch apply after Cadence review

5. **Measure impact** (post-apply):
   - Query agent_runs: avg_before, avg_after (14-day window before/after patch applied_at)
   - Update training_patches: impact_score = avg_after - avg_before
   - If regression >10%: trigger auto-rollback (restore from rollback_content, set applied=false)

6. **Generate changelog:**
   ```markdown
   # Training Changelog — Cycle [cycle_id]
   Date: [timestamp]
   Triggered by: [trigger type]
   
   ## Patches Applied:
   1. [agent] — [patch_type]: [summary]
      - Section: [target]
      - Source: [signal type]
      - Impact: +[points] (or rolled back)
   
   ## Signals Consumed:
   [list all signal IDs processed]
   ```

7. **Report to Cadence & Yash:**
   - Summary: patches created, applied, impact scores
   - Any rollbacks executed
   - Open incidents/blockers

## VI. KNOWN LIMITS & CONSTRAINTS

### Current Limits (Scalability for 40-50 agents)

| Constraint | Current | Challenge at 40-50 agents | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Weekly review time** | ~30min (22-27 agents) | Will scale to 45-60min | Parallelize peer comparisons; cache peer_avg |
| **Nightly recompute** | ~15min (SQL queries) | Will scale to 30-45min | Index optimization; incremental updates |
| **Training cycles per week** | 2-3 cycles | Could spike to 5-7 | Batch P2-P5, apply async after Cadence review |
| **Probation agents** | 0-2 at a time | Could be 3-5 simultaneous | Witness parallelization for 10-run monitoring |
| **PIP capacity** | 1-2 at a time | Could be 2-4 concurrent | Cadence cycle can handle ≤5 simultaneous |
| **Agent .md files** | ~30 files, ~200KB total | Will grow to ~50 files, ~350KB | Compaction; move Tier 2 skills to separate files |
| **Supabase rows** | Manageable (<10K rows in agent_ops) | Will grow to 50K+/month | Add data retention policy; archive old runs |

### Scaling Requirements

To support 40-50 agents without breaking infrastructure:

1. **Supabase indices:** Add on agent_id, created_at for agent_runs table (currently missing)
2. **Nightly caching:** Cache peer_avg scores in Redis; recompute only if >12h stale
3. **Skill index compression:** Move skill details to separate table; keep agent.skills as JSON keys only
4. **Training pipeline batching:** Group P2-P5 into single weekly cycle (not individual cycles per signal)
5. **Witness parallelization:** Query antipattern signatures in parallel (current: sequential)
6. **Probation watch:** Background job instead of daily sweep (reduces 03:00 UTC load)
7. **PIP deadline enforcement:** Cron job to auto-close expired PIPs (not just Cadence review)
8. **Cost tracking:** Archive cost_logs older than 90 days to reduce table bloat

### No Hard Limits Found

The schema itself has **no hard max** on agent count. Constraints are:
- **Practical:** Weekly review time (solvable with caching)
- **Bandwidth:** Supabase query performance (solvable with indices)
- **Observability:** Too much data per agent (solvable with sampling/retention policy)

**Recommendation:** Scale to 50 agents is technically safe. Beyond 50, consider sharding the agent-ops database by department.

## VIII. TRAINING MECHANISMS IN DETAIL

### How Mira Extracts Lessons

**Post-Build Trigger:**
1. Build completes → Mira reads `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-validated-patterns.md` (validation baseline)
2. Mira analyzes all agent outputs against quality standards
3. Mira identifies:
   - Patterns that worked (new learning)
   - Antipatterns that appeared
   - Performance metrics per feature
4. Mira inserts into `training_signals` table:
   - event_type='lessons_extracted'
   - Payload: lessons array with type, description, affected_agent_ids, confidence_level
5. Mira updates `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/` with new patterns
6. Mira inserts into `agent_events`: type='pattern_extracted'

**Tutor picks up signals** from training_signals WHERE event_type='lessons_extracted' AND processed=false

### How Mira Validates Output

Quality scoring (must score ≥3/5 to store):

| Dimension | 1 (Reject) | 3 (Acceptable) | 5 (Excellent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Specificity** | "Be careful" | "Add null check for X" | "When fetching user.profile, always check `if (!profile)` because Supabase RLS returns null" |
| **Actionability** | Generic advice | "Add index to foreign keys" | "Create `idx_results_job_id` on results(job_id) — reduces 800ms to 12ms on 10K+ rows" |
| **Evidence** | No source | "Found in project X" | "Project: Rankora, Agent: Sage, Date: 2025-01-15, Context: P0 perf bug" |
| **Scope** | "Always do this" | "For SaaS apps" | "For Stack A (Next.js+Supabase) with >1000 users, do this because..." |

Mira also maintains **knowledge graph** with relationships:
- DEPENDS_ON: A requires B to work
- SUPERSEDES: A replaces B (newer)
- CONFLICTS_WITH: A and B can't both be true
- EXTENDS: A adds to B
- SCOPED_TO: A only applies when [condition]

5. **Switch to Supabase primary:**
   - Roster reads/writes PRIMARY to Supabase
   - registry.json becomes weekly export only

6. **Onboard 10-15 more specialized agents:**
   - Stagger across 2 weeks (avoid probation surge)
   - Ensure Witness doesn't bottleneck

7. **Scale training to auto-batching:**
   - Weekly training cycles instead of per-signal
   - Cadence bulk-approves patches

### Phase 3: Weeks 5-6

8. **Full roster of 40-50 agents:**
   - Monitor nightly recompute (should be <30min)
   - Monitor weekly review (should be <45min)
   - Validate no regressions

9. **Tune thresholds:**
   - Composite score weights may need adjustment at scale
   - Peer average calculations become more meaningful
   - PIP thresholds may need to tighten

10. **Archive legacy registry.json:**
    - Move to `~/.claude/org/_archive/registry.json.2026-04-30`
    - Keep for historical reference only

### Critical Success Factors

1. **Supabase indices:** Without them, nightly recompute will slow >2x at 50 agents
2. **Training batching:** Weekly cycles instead of per-signal prevent training explosion
3. **Witness parallelization:** Daily sweep must stay under 15min even at 50 agents
4. **Yash feedback loop:** User/feedback.md must stay current (highest priority)
5. **Skill decay policy:** Need automated archival of patterns unused >90 days (prevents stale knowledge)

---

## SUMMARY: Architecture is Solid, Ready to Scale

**The Boldteq HR infrastructure is comprehensively designed and well-documented.** Current bottlenecks are:
- Supabase not yet activated (blocking live data flow)
- Training still manual per-signal (should batch weekly)
- No automated PIP deadline enforcement

**For scaling from ~25 to 40-50 agents, the infrastructure supports it WITHOUT major rewrites.** Just needs:
1. Supabase deployment + indices
2. Training pipeline batching
3. Witness async/parallel processing
4. Skill decay automation

The lifecycle (hire → probation → active → PIP → retire) is iron-clad. Training mechanisms (patches + rollback) are surgical and trackable. Performance tracking (composite scores + peer comparison) is data-driven and fair.

**Recommendation:** Proceed with scaling. Activate Supabase first. Then hire in cohorts of 5 agents per week to avoid overwhelming Witness/Cadence.

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive information. Let me create a structured report in markdown format.

## Boldteq HR/Training Infrastructure — Comprehensive Research Report

Based on thorough exploration of `~/.claude/agents/`, `~/.claude/org/`, `~/.claude/memory/`, and the Supabase agent-ops schema, here's the exact current state of the agent lifecycle, training, and HR infrastructure:

---

### CURRENT STATE SNAPSHOT

**Agent Roster:** 30 agents (27 production + 3 system/audit) across 6 departments
- Executive (3): Rex, Arya, Cadence, Echo, Nova, Quill
- Engineering (10+): Koda, Riko, Sage, Bolt, Dato, Hawk, Vex, etc.
- Research (4): Nova, Atlas, Scout, Audit
- Creative (2): Quill, Pixel
- Growth (3): Echo, Harvest, Orbit  
- HR (6): Cadence, Roster, Witness, Forge, Tutor, Mira

**Planned Expansion:** From ~25-27 to 40-50 specialized agents (per your brief)

---

## I. EXACT AGENT LIFECYCLE: HIRE → PROBATION → ACTIVE → PIP → RETIRE

### Step-by-Step Hiring (New Agent Creation)

**Step 1: Capability Gap Detection** (`Roster` → `Forge`)
- Roster detects gaps via Supabase query:
  - Overloaded agents (>10 runs/month + >2 avg retries)
  - Delegation bottlenecks (>40% of tasks to one agent)
  - Task type failures (same task >3x with ≠ SUCCESS)
  - Retry spikes (>20% failure rate per task type)
  - Zero coverage on core skills (audit, deployment, monitoring, etc.)
  - Yash explicit feedback in `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md`
- Gap record inserted into `capability_gaps` table with detected_at timestamp

**Step 2: Agent Design** (`Forge` creates spec)
- 11-section mandatory spec (.md file):
  1. YAML frontmatter (name, title, department, tier, reportsTo, model, color)
  2. Role & Responsibility (why this agent exists)
  3. Core Processes (3+ processes defined)
  4. Inputs/Outputs schema (JSON examples)
  5. Auto-Fix Loop (5 retries table)
  6. Smart Defaults (for ambiguous inputs)
  7. Handoff Contracts (upstream/downstream expectations)
  8. Supabase Integration (tables read/written, events)
  9. Self-Validation Checklist (runnable acceptance criteria)
  10. Anti-Patterns (5-10 explicit "never do" statements)
  11. Completion Proof (specific done criteria)
- Validation checklist auto-checks before deployment (missing section = rejection)
- Token count must be <4000

**Step 3: Auto-Deploy to Probation** (NO manual Yash approval at this stage)
- Forge INSERT agent into `agents` table with `level=1` (Probation), `status='deployed'`
- Forge INSERT `agent_created` event to `agent_events` table
- Forge SAVE .md file to `~/.claude/agents/[name].md`
- **CRITICAL:** Supabase write happens BEFORE file save (rollback safety: if file write fails, agent is deleted from DB)
- Witness automatically starts watching (10-run observation period)

**Step 4: Probation Watch** (Witness monitors 10 runs)
- Witness tracks: composite_score trend, success rate, antipatterns
- After 10 runs: Witness inserts `probation_review_ready` event to `agent_events`
- Witness DOES NOT promote directly (only flags for Cadence)

**Step 5: Cadence Review & Promotion Decision** (Monday weekly review)
- Cadence checks agent's 14-day composite score vs. peer average
- Cadence reviews flagged new agents in weekly cycle
- Decision: **Promote to Active (level=2)** OR **extend probation** OR **retire**
- UPDATE `agents` table with new level, INSERT promotion event to `agent_events`
- Cadence requires Yash approval for promotions (via `user/feedback.md` override)

**Step 6: Active Status** (agent can receive delegations, run production tasks)
- Agent now at `level=2`, ready for standard workload
- Can be assigned to complex tasks with mentorship if needed

---

### Training & Skill Development Pipeline

**Training Mechanism: Patches + Changelogs** (`Tutor` orchestrates)

Tutor does NOT edit agent .md files directly. Instead:
1. **Receives training signals** from 4 sources:
   - P0: Yash corrections (detected by Witness from `yash_overrides` table)
   - P1: Witness antipatterns (3+ occurrences = high priority)
   - P2: Mira lessons (post-build extraction)
   - P3: Cadence requests (skill gap training, pre-approved)
   - P4: Forge gaps (new agent onboarding)
   - P5: Trend synthesis (weekly market patterns, propose to Yash)

2. **Creates Training Cycle** (record in `training_cycles` table):
   - cycle_id, triggered_by, trigger_priority, signals_consumed, patch_count, impact_measured

3. **Generates Training Patches** (per agent per cycle in `training_patches` table):
   - Patch types: anti_pattern | smart_default | auto_fix | pattern_addition | update_existing | remove_stale
   - Each patch stores: content_added, rollback_content (for safety), section_target
   - **Rollback hash:** Git commit hash of memory state before patch (enables safe rollback)

4. **Applies Patches** (conditional on priority):
   - P0 (Yash): Apply immediately, no review
   - P1-P2: Stage for Cadence quick-review, apply within 1h of approval
   - P3: Auto-approved by Cadence (batch into weekly cycle)
   - P4-P5: Stage for weekly approval

5. **Measures Impact** (post-apply):
   - Query agent_runs before/after patch applied_at
   - Calculate avg_composite_score change: `avg_after - avg_before`
   - Auto-rollback if regression >10% (`avg_after < avg_before - 10`)
   - Update training_patches with impact_score

6. **Generates Changelog** (with full traceability):
   - Section modified, source signal, rollback available, impact score
   - Emitted to `~/.claude/memory/training/` (structured markdown with timestamps)

**What is a "Patch"?**
- A surgical edit to one agent's .md file, targeting one section
- Backed by rollback content (original text before edit)
- Linked to source signals (Mira lesson, Witness antipattern, Yash correction)
- Immutable record in training_patches table with applied_at timestamp

---

### Step-by-Step Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)

**Opening a PIP** (`Cadence` decides)

Cadence opens when:
- Composite score <peer average for 14+ consecutive days, OR
- 3+ ANTIPATTERN classifications in 30 days, OR
- Yash flags in `feedback.md`

Process:
1. INSERT into `pip_records` table:
   - agent_id, opened_at, deadline (NOW() + 14 days), reason, metrics_at_open (JSON snapshot)
2. INSERT event to `agent_events` with type='pip_opened'
3. **Duration:** Exactly 14 days. No extension. One cycle only.

**Closing a PIP**

When deadline passes or improvement shown:
1. Query metrics_at_close (same structure as metrics_at_open, for comparison)
2. UPDATE `pip_records`: status='closed', closed_at=NOW(), outcome='resolved' | 'demoted' | 'retired'
3. If demoted: UPDATE agent level = level - 1
4. If retired: UPDATE agent status = 'retired'
5. INSERT event to `agent_events` with type='pip_closed'

---

### Retirement (Soft Only, Never Delete)

**Trigger conditions:**
- Agent status='deployed' AND lastRunAt < now() - 90 days (zero usage)
- Cadence decision: PIP expired without improvement
- Yash explicit directive

**Workflow:**
1. Flag for review: UPDATE status='training' (soft deprecation)
2. Notify stakeholders: Query delegation_graph to prepare handoff
3. Move .md file: `mv ~/.claude/agents/[name].md ~/.claude/agents/_retired/[name]_[date].md`
4. Mark retired: UPDATE agents SET status='retired'
5. INSERT event: type='agent_retired'

Agent .md files are NEVER deleted—only archived to `_retired/` folder. Can be recalled.

---

## II. WHAT DATA DOES WITNESS COLLECT & WHERE?

**Core: Witness = Daily Run Logger + Classifier** (runs at 03:00 UTC)

### Run Logging (Every Agent Execution)

At task **START:**
- INSERT into `agent_events`: event_type='task_started', with task_type, input_summary, triggered_by

At task **END:**
- Compute composite_score inline: 
  ```
  (gate_pass_rate × 40) + (first_try_success × 30) + (rework_factor × 20) + (override_factor × 10)
  ```
  - gate_pass_rate = gatesPassed / (gatesPassed + gatesFailed)
  - first_try = 1.0 if no retries, 0.0 otherwise
  - rework_factor = max(0, 1.0 - (retries × 0.2))
  - override_factor = 1.0 - (overrides_in_14_days / total_runs_in_14_days)
  - Result: 0–100 scale

- INSERT into `agent_runs` table:
  - agent_id, run_id, task_type, classification, gates_passed, gates_failed
  - first_try_success, rework_cycles, composite_score, duration_ms
  - token_count, cost_usd, yash_override

### Run Classification Logic

Witness assigns classification based on run data:
- **SUCCESS** (score ≥80): All gates passed, ≤1 retry, no override, no antipatterns
- **PARTIAL** (50-79): Passed but needed retries, some gate issues, minor overrides
- **FAILURE** (<50): Gates failed, significant rework, OR matched antipattern
- **TIMEOUT**: duration_ms > WALL_CLOCK_CAP for agent's class
- **REGRESSION**: composite_score dropped >20 points from agent's 30-day rolling avg
- **ANTIPATTERN**: Output matches known signature in `proposed_patterns` table (pattern_type='avoid', status='approved')
- **ESCALATED**: Agent returned with escalation flag OR hit cost/time cap

### Antipattern Detection (During Classification)

For each run, Witness queries `proposed_patterns` WHERE pattern_type='avoid' AND status='approved':
- If match found: UPDATE run's classification='ANTIPATTERN'
- INSERT into `incidents` table: incident_type='antipattern'
- INSERT into `agent_events`: type='antipattern_detected' with evidence
- If NEW antipattern (not yet approved): INSERT into `proposed_patterns` with status='pending' for Yash review

**Known Antipatterns Table:**

| Signature | Pattern | Agents | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| any_type_ts | `any\s+(type\|:)` | All | TypeScript `any` type in production |
| missing_rls | No RLS policy on new table | Koda, Dato | Missing row-level security |
| hardcoded_secret | `SUPABASE_\|API_KEY\|TOKEN` | All | Secret in code, not env |
| console_log_prod | `console\.(log\|debug\|warn)` | All | console.log in production code |
| npm_instead_pnpm | `npm install` (Stack A) | Koda, Riko | Should use `pnpm install` |

### PIP & Promotion Recommendations (In-Session)

After daily sweep, Witness scans last 30 days per agent:

**PIP Candidate** (INSERT into `incidents` with severity='S1'):
- Success rate (last 20 runs) <0.70, OR
- Antipattern count (last 30 days) ≥3, OR
- Same regression type ≥2 times, OR
- Yash flagged in `yash_overrides` table

**Promotion Candidate** (INSERT into `incidents` with severity='S2'):
- Current level <expected level from performance
- Success rate ≥0.85 (last 20 runs)
- Antipattern count (last 30 days) = 0
- Patterns authored ≥1 (for level ≥3 agents)

Cadence picks up these incidents in Monday weekly review.

### Probation Watch (10-run Window)

When new agent deployed (level=1), Witness auto-monitors:
```sql
SELECT agent_id, COUNT(runs) as run_count, AVG(composite_score) as avg_score
FROM agent_runs 
WHERE agent_id=$1 AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY agent_id
HAVING COUNT(runs) >= 10
```

After 10 runs, Witness inserts `probation_review_ready` event (NOT a promotion decision—flags for Cadence).

### Data Destinations

All Witness data flows to Supabase `agent-ops` database:
- **Writes:** agent_runs, agent_events, incidents, agent_pips_active (when flagged)
- **Reads:** agents table, agent_runs history, proposed_patterns, yash_overrides
- **No direct edits to .md files** (read-only on agent code)

---

## III. CADENCE'S MONDAY REVIEW (09:00 UTC WEEKLY)

**What Cadence Actually Does (Not Theory—Exact Decisions)**

### Pre-Review Data Load

1. Load `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md` (highest priority)
2. Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/agent-ops-schema.md`
3. Load `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-agent-mindset.md`

### Review Execution Order

**Strict sequence (no skipping):**

1. **Query all agents:** SELECT * FROM agents WHERE status IN ('deployed', 'probation', 'training')
2. **Fetch 14-day scores:** Query agent_runs grouped by agent_id, created_at > NOW() - 14 days, compute avg composite_score per agent
3. **Calculate peer averages:** For each level (1, 2, 3, 4), compute avg score = SUM(composite_scores) / COUNT(agents at same level)
4. **Classify each agent** against 6 decision types:
   - PROMOTE (if composite_score > peer_avg AND runs ≥5 AND no active PIP AND no Yash override in 7 days AND no ANTIPATTERN in 30 days)
   - SCALE (keep at level, increase task complexity)
   - STEADY (continue pace)
   - TRAIN (enroll in Tutor cycle for specific skill gaps)
   - PIP (open 14-day performance improvement plan)
   - RETIRE (mark status='retired')

5. **Insert review records:** INSERT into `agent_reviews` table (one per agent per period):
   - agent_id, review_date, period_start (now() - 7d), period_end (now())
   - classification, rationale, peer_avg_score, agent_avg_score
   - decision_approved=false (awaiting Yash approval)

6. **Handle promotions:**
   - For agents with classification='PROMOTE':
     - Cadence MUST have Yash approval (check `feedback.md` for overrides)
     - UPDATE agents table: level = level + 1
     - INSERT event to agent_events: type='agent_promoted', payload includes new level

7. **Handle PIPs:**
   - For agents with classification='PIP':
     - INSERT into pip_records with deadline=NOW() + 14 days
     - INSERT event: type='agent_pip_opened'

8. **Handle training requests:**
   - For agents with classification='TRAIN':
     - INSERT into training_requests: agent_id, skill_gap, priority='P3', reviewed=true
     - Tutor picks up in next weekly batch (auto-approved)

9. **Generate summary report:**
   - Count of PROMOTE, SCALE, STEADY, TRAIN, PIP, RETIRE decisions
   - List of agents changed, previous status → new status
   - Open PIPs with deadlines
   - Save to `~/.claude/org/reviews/2026-W[week].json`

### Example Output (from 2026-W16 review)

```json
{
  "week": "2026-W16",
  "reviewedAt": "2026-04-13T17:58:30.933Z",
  "director": "cadence",
  "promotions": [],
  "pipsOpened": [],
  "pipsClosed": [],
  "retirements": [],
  "newHires": [],
  "capabilityGaps": [...]
}
```

**Note:** Week 16 shows NO promotions/PIPs (clean week, all agents steady).

---

## IV. CAPABILITY GAP DETECTION FLOW (ROSTER → FORGE)

**Exact Detection Process**

### Roster's Nightly Recompute (02:00 UTC)

Roster runs SQL 5-step pipeline:

**Step 1: Compute run-based metrics** (last 90 days)
```sql
SELECT 
  agent_id,
  COUNT(*) as run_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification='SUCCESS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) as success_rate,
  AVG(composite_score) as avg_composite_score,
  AVG(duration_ms) as avg_duration_ms,
  MAX(created_at) as last_run_at
FROM agent_runs
WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
GROUP BY agent_id
```

**Step 2: Recompute skills** (90-day rolling window, min 2 hits per skill)
```sql
WITH skill_scores AS (
  SELECT 
    agent_id,
    skill_key,
    AVG((composite_score)) / 100.0 as score,
    COUNT(*) as hits
  FROM pattern_usage
  LEFT JOIN agent_runs ...
  WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
  GROUP BY agent_id, skill_key
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
UPDATE agents SET 
  skills = (JSON object with skill_key → {score, hits})
  weaknesses = (array of skills where score < 0.3)
```

**Step 3: Recompute experience & level** (YoE calculated from run age + pattern authorship)
- Level 1 = Probation (≤10 runs)
- Level 2 = Active (11-50 runs)
- Level 3 = Expert (51+ runs + patterns authored ≥1)
- Level 4 = Architect (100+ runs + patterns authored ≥3 + strategic contributions)

**Step 4: Detect drift** (disk vs. database)
- Read all `~/.claude/agents/*.md` files
- Compare against agents table
- Agents on disk but not in DB → INSERT with auto-generated defaults
- Agents in DB but not on disk → UPDATE status='archived'
- Frontmatter mismatches → INSERT into drift_log with eventType='metadata_mismatch'

**Step 5: Rebuild skill index** (cached JSON)
```sql
WITH skill_rankings AS (
  SELECT 
    skill_key,
    agent_id,
    (skills->skill_key->>'score')::float as score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY skill_key ORDER BY score DESC) as rank
  FROM agents
  WHERE status IN ('active', 'deployed', 'probation')
)
UPDATE agents SET skill_leaderboard = (JSON object with skill rankings)
```

### Gap Detection: Scoring System

When Roster checks "Can we handle this task?"

**Input:**
```json
{
  "brief": "Build distributed tracing observability SaaS with vector databases",
  "requiredSkills": ["observability", "vector-db", "saas", "distributed-systems"],
  "isHighStakes": false
}
```

**SQL assessment:**
```sql
WITH skill_assessment AS (
  SELECT 
    skill_key,
    MAX((skills->skill_key->>'score')::float) as best_score,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN (skills->skill_key->>'score')::float >= 0.7 THEN 1 END) as covered_agents
  FROM agents
  WHERE status IN ('active', 'deployed')
    AND skills ? (skill_key)
  GROUP BY skill_key
)
SELECT 
  skill_key,
  best_score,
  covered_agents,
  CASE 
    WHEN best_score >= 0.8 THEN 'covered'
    WHEN best_score >= 0.5 THEN 'trainable'
    WHEN best_score >= 0.3 THEN 'weak'
    ELSE 'uncovered'
  END as coverage_status
FROM skill_assessment
```

**Decision logic:**

| Coverage | Recommendation | Action |
|---|---|---|
| All skills ≥0.7 + 1 agent covers all | **proceed** | Assign to best agent |
| All skills ≥0.4 + trainable agent exists | **train-[agent]** | Route to Tutor for targeted training |
| Any skill <0.4 | **hire** | Signal Forge to design new agent |

**Confidence score:**
```
(AVG(best_score) + covered_agent_count / total_active_agents) / 2
```

### Forge's Monthly Gap Detection** (1st of month, 02:00 UTC)

Forge queries Supabase for signals:

| Signal | Query | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Overloaded agent** | runs >10/month + avg retry >2 | Yes | Specialize role |
| **Bottleneck** | delegation to_agent >40% of all tasks | Yes | Create load-balancing agent |
| **Task gap** | same task type fails >3x in 30d | Yes | Create specialist |
| **Retry spike** | task type failure rate >20% in 14d | Yes | Create expert |
| **Yash feedback** | grep "missing", "wish", "need agent" in feedback.md | Any mention | Highest priority |
| **Zero coverage** | skill with no agents (skill_score >0.4) | Any core skill | Urgent hire |
| **Obsolete agent** | last_run_at >90 days ago | Yes | Flag for retirement |

**Output:**
- Gap report saved to `~/.claude/memory/agent-evolution/gap-report-YYYY-MM.md`
- New agents auto-deployed to probation (no approval gate at deploy time)
- Cadence reviews in next weekly review

---

## V. TRAINING PIPELINE IN DETAIL

### Tutor's 4 Triggers (Priority Order)

| Priority | Trigger | Response Time | Review Gate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Yash correction | Immediate | None (auto-apply) | Witness detects in yash_overrides |
| **P1** | Witness antipattern (3+/30d) | Within 1h | Cadence quick-review | Witness incident |
| **P2** | Mira lessons (post-build) | Next day | Cadence review | training_signals (event_type='lessons_extracted') |
| **P3** | Cadence requests | Next weekly batch | Already approved | training_requests (reviewed=true) |
| **P4** | Forge gaps (new onboarding) | Next weekly batch | Cadence batch approval | agents table (status='probation') |
| **P5** | Trend synthesis | Weekly | Yash approval needed | Manual synthesis from Mira patterns |

### Tutor's Workflow

1. **Create training cycle:** INSERT into `training_cycles`
   - cycle_id (unique), triggered_by, status='in_progress'

2. **For each signal:** INSERT into `training_patches`
   - agent_id, patch_type (anti_pattern | smart_default | auto_fix | pattern_addition | update_existing)
   - section_target (path in agent .md), content_added, rollback_content
   - applied=false initially

3. **Stage for review** (P1-P2 only):
   - UPDATE training_patches SET status='staged_for_review'
   - Send summary to Cadence: count, priority, agents affected

4. **Apply patches** (conditional):
   - P0: Read agent .md, use Edit tool to surgically update section, update DB: applied=true, applied_at=NOW()
   - P1-P2: Wait for Cadence approval → then apply
   - P3: Auto-apply in weekly batch
   - P4-P5: Batch apply after Cadence review

5. **Measure impact** (post-apply):
   - Query agent_runs: avg_before, avg_after (14-day window before/after patch applied_at)
   - Update training_patches: impact_score = avg_after - avg_before
   - If regression >10%: trigger auto-rollback (restore from rollback_content, set applied=false)

6. **Generate changelog:**
   ```markdown
   # Training Changelog — Cycle [cycle_id]
   Date: [timestamp]
   Triggered by: [trigger type]
   
   ## Patches Applied:
   1. [agent] — [patch_type]: [summary]
      - Section: [target]
      - Source: [signal type]
      - Impact: +[points] (or rolled back)
   
   ## Signals Consumed:
   [list all signal IDs processed]
   ```

7. **Report to Cadence & Yash:**
   - Summary: patches created, applied, impact scores
   - Any rollbacks executed
   - Open incidents/blockers

---

## VI. KNOWN LIMITS & CONSTRAINTS

### Current Limits (Scalability for 40-50 agents)

| Constraint | Current | Challenge at 40-50 agents | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Weekly review time** | ~30min (22-27 agents) | Will scale to 45-60min | Parallelize peer comparisons; cache peer_avg |
| **Nightly recompute** | ~15min (SQL queries) | Will scale to 30-45min | Index optimization; incremental updates |
| **Training cycles per week** | 2-3 cycles | Could spike to 5-7 | Batch P2-P5, apply async after Cadence review |
| **Probation agents** | 0-2 at a time | Could be 3-5 simultaneous | Witness parallelization for 10-run monitoring |
| **PIP capacity** | 1-2 at a time | Could be 2-4 concurrent | Cadence cycle can handle ≤5 simultaneous |
| **Agent .md files** | ~30 files, ~200KB total | Will grow to ~50 files, ~350KB | Compaction; move Tier 2 skills to separate files |
| **Supabase rows** | Manageable (<10K rows in agent_ops) | Will grow to 50K+/month | Add data retention policy; archive old runs |

### Scaling Requirements

To support 40-50 agents without breaking infrastructure:

1. **Supabase indices:** Add on agent_id, created_at for agent_runs table (currently missing)
2. **Nightly caching:** Cache peer_avg scores in Redis; recompute only if >12h stale
3. **Skill index compression:** Move skill details to separate table; keep agent.skills as JSON keys only

## VIII. TRAINING MECHANISMS IN DETAIL

### How Mira Extracts Lessons

**Post-Build Trigger:**
1. Build completes → Mira reads `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/production-validated-patterns.md` (validation baseline)
2. Mira analyzes all agent outputs against quality standards
3. Mira identifies:
   - Patterns that worked (new learning)
   - Antipatterns that appeared
   - Performance metrics per feature
4. Mira inserts into `training_signals` table:
   - event_type='lessons_extracted'
   - Payload: lessons array with type, description, affected_agent_ids, confidence_level
5. Mira updates `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/` with new patterns
6. Mira inserts into `agent_events`: type='pattern_extracted'

**Tutor picks up signals** from training_signals WHERE event_type='lessons_extracted' AND processed=false

### How Mira Validates Output

Quality scoring (must score ≥3/5 to store):

| Dimension | 1 (Reject) | 3 (Acceptable) | 5 (Excellent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Specificity** | "Be careful" | "Add null check for X" | "When fetching user.profile, always check `if (!profile)` because Supabase RLS returns null" |
| **Actionability** | Generic advice | "Add index to foreign keys" | "Create `idx_results_job_id` on results(job_id) — reduces 800ms to 12ms on 10K+ rows" |
| **Evidence** | No source | "Found in project X" | "Project: Rankora, Agent: Sage, Date: 2025-01-15, Context: P0 perf bug" |
| **Scope** | "Always do this" | "For SaaS apps" | "For Stack A (Next.js+Supabase) with >1000 users, do this because..." |

Mira also maintains **knowledge graph** with relationships:
- DEPENDS_ON: A requires B to work
- SUPERSEDES: A replaces B (newer)
- CONFLICTS_WITH: A and B can't both be true
- EXTENDS: A adds to B
- SCOPED_TO: A only applies when [condition]

# HR Plan: Scale Agent Workforce 30 → 54 in 6 Weeks

## Context

Today the Boldteq Software Factory runs **30 agents** across 6 departments. Three are critically overloaded (Koda, Quill, Rex), and three core capability blocks are missing: **stack-specific engineering depth** (3 stacks share one Koda), **deep design specialization** (only Vega + Pixel for all UI/UX), and **CRO mastery** (no agent owns conversion strategy).

The factory's mission requires bulk SaaS shipping across 3 stacks: **Next.js + Supabase + Railway**, **Shopify Native**, and **Shopify External**. Every project also needs **Resend transactional email** and **40%+ conversion** marketing/ecom pages — neither of which has a deep specialist today.

This plan locks in **24 net-new specialist agents** + **4 decompositions of overloaded agents**, executed in **6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents** under a strengthened HR team. Every new agent is narrow-by-design to maximize per-task token efficiency: each agent loads only the memory/skills it owns, never the full org's knowledge base.

**Boldteq B2B agency operations are deferred to v2** (post 5 paying clients on boldteq.com). All 24 new hires serve internal product velocity first.

**End-state:** 54 agents, every routing decision touches the most-specialized agent, token waste drops ~40%.

---

## Locked Decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Total scale | 30 → 54 agents (24 net new + 4 decompositions) |
| Pace | 6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents/week + Week 0 prep |
| Engineering org | 3 stack-specific pods (5 roles each) — repurpose existing for Pod A, hire new for Pods B + C |
| Design org | Bundle of 4: Ecom UI, Dashboard, Design System, Figma Synth (JSX→.fig) |
| CRO org | Bundle of 5 under new CRO Lead: Lead, Decoder, Hero/CTA, Landing CRO, Ecom CRO |
| Email org | 2 agents: Postmark (Resend infra) + Lifecycle (CRO email sequences) |
| Decomposition order | Week 0 (before any new hire) — split Quill, narrow Koda/Vega/Rex |
| HR readiness | Week 0 curriculum upgrade for Cadence/Tutor/Witness/Forge + Supabase agent-ops activation |
| CRO methodology | Top 50 brand audit upfront + weekly Decoder + on-demand niche teardowns |
| Figma workflow | JSX-first → Figma Synth converts to .fig as deliverable artifact |
| Boldteq B2B agency | Deferred to v2 |

---

## Week-by-Week Cohort Schedule

### Week 0 — Foundations (NO new agents; pure prep)

**Decompositions (Forge edits existing agent .md files):**
1. **Split Quill** → Quill (marketing copy, brand voice, landing/email/social only) + 2 new agents to be hired (Serif, Docsmith) in week 5.
2. **Narrow Koda** → Pod A Backend specialist (Next.js API routes, server components, integrations only). Drops: design, testing, research, database design (all delegated).
3. **Narrow Vega** → Design Department Lead only (delegates execution to the 4 new design specialists). Owns: cross-pod design standards, design review, escalations.
4. **Narrow Rex** → Strategic commander only (portfolio decisions, 30/90-day verdicts, dept VPs mentoring). Drops: hands-on technical execution.

**HR strength training (Mira writes curriculum):**
- Cadence: weekly review protocol at 50-agent scale, peer-avg caching, decision rubrics
- Tutor: curriculum design framework, batch training cycles, patch-impact measurement
- Witness: probation-watch parallelization, antipattern signature library, classification edge cases
- Forge: spec writing template enforcement, capability-gap detection queries, probation-rollback protocol

**Infrastructure (Bolt deploys):**
- Supabase agent-ops schema deployed to production (13 tables from `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/agent-ops-schema.md`)
- Indices added: `idx_agent_runs_agent_id_created`, `idx_agent_runs_classification`, `idx_incidents_agent_id`, `idx_training_patches_cycle_id`
- RLS policies enabled (service-role only)
- Roster begins dual-write: `registry.json` + `agents` table for 7-day verification

**Existing agent reassignments:**
- Koda → renamed `pod-a-backend` (or kept as Koda, narrowed mandate)
- Dato → assigned to Pod A as DB specialist
- Luna → assigned to Pod A as Tester (cross-pod test mentor for Pods B + C)
- Sage → assigned to Pod A as Reviewer (cross-pod review mentor for Pods B + C)

| `pod-b-db` | Prisma schema, migrations, indexes, multi-shop tenancy | Dato (mentor) | shopify-app.md + Prisma docs |

| `pod-b-reviewer` | Code review specific to Shopify Native: Polaris compliance, GraphQL N+1, billing edge cases | Sage (mentor) | shopify-app.md + sage's review checklist |

**Witness:** Begins 10-run probation watch on all 5.

---

### Week 2 — Cohort 2: Shopify External Pod (5 agents)

| New Agent | Mandate | Reports To | Memory Load |

| `pod-c-frontend` | Standalone Shopify-integrated UI (non-embedded), customer-facing flows | Arya | shopify-app.md + external-specific patterns |

**Witness:** Probation watch on Cohort 1 ongoing (mid-window). Cohort 2 watch begins.

---

### Week 3 — Cohort 3: Design Specialists + Pod A Frontend (5 agents)

| New Agent | Mandate | Reports To | Memory Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| `elio` (Ecom UI Designer) | Storefront UI, PDPs, cart/checkout, collections, ecom interaction patterns | Vega | design/ + ecom patterns |

- Decode top 50 brands (10 SaaS: Linear, Stripe, Notion, Vercel, Framer, Posthog, Clerk, Resend, Supabase, Webflow / 10 Ecom: Shopify, Allbirds, Glossier, Casper, Brooklinen, Warby Parker, Away, Bombas, Outdoor Voices, Gymshark / 10 B2B: Salesforce, Hubspot, Intercom, Asana, Slack, Figma, Loom, Calendly, Zapier, Airtable / 10 DTC: Liquid Death, Athletic Greens, Dollar Shave, Manscaped, Olipop, Magic Spoon, Caraway, Our Place, Fishwife, Graza / 10 Mobile-first: Robinhood, Cash App, Duolingo, Headspace, Calm, Strava, Spotify, TikTok, Instagram, BeReal)
- Output: `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/cro-decoded-patterns.md` (sectioned by hero, social proof, pricing, onboarding, CTA, urgency, friction reduction)

# HR Plan: Scale Agent Workforce 30 → 54 in 6 Weeks

## Context

Today the Boldteq Software Factory runs **30 agents** across 6 departments. Three are critically overloaded (Koda, Quill, Rex), and three core capability blocks are missing: **stack-specific engineering depth** (3 stacks share one Koda), **deep design specialization** (only Vega + Pixel for all UI/UX), and **CRO mastery** (no agent owns conversion strategy).

The factory's mission requires bulk SaaS shipping across 3 stacks: **Next.js + Supabase + Railway**, **Shopify Native**, and **Shopify External**. Every project also needs **Resend transactional email** and **40%+ conversion** marketing/ecom pages — neither of which has a deep specialist today.

This plan locks in **24 net-new specialist agents** + **4 decompositions of overloaded agents**, executed in **6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents** under a strengthened HR team. Every new agent is narrow-by-design to maximize per-task token efficiency: each agent loads only the memory/skills it owns, never the full org's knowledge base.

**Boldteq B2B agency operations are deferred to v2** (post 5 paying clients on boldteq.com). All 24 new hires serve internal product velocity first.

**End-state:** 54 agents, every routing decision touches the most-specialized agent, token waste drops ~40%.

---

## Locked Decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Total scale | 30 → 54 agents (24 net new + 4 decompositions) |
| Pace | 6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents/week + Week 0 prep |
| Engineering org | 3 stack-specific pods (5 roles each) — repurpose existing for Pod A, hire new for Pods B + C |
| Design org | Bundle of 4: Ecom UI, Dashboard, Design System, Figma Synth (JSX→.fig) |
| CRO org | Bundle of 5 under new CRO Lead: Lead, Decoder, Hero/CTA, Landing CRO, Ecom CRO |
| Email org | 2 agents: Postmark (Resend infra) + Lifecycle (CRO email sequences) |

| HR readiness | Week 0 curriculum upgrade for Cadence/Tutor/Witness/Forge + Supabase agent-ops activation |
| CRO methodology | Top 50 brand audit upfront + weekly Decoder + on-demand niche teardowns |

## Context

Today the Boldteq Software Factory runs **30 agents** across 6 departments. Today the Boldteq Software Factory runs **30 agents** across 6 departments. # HR Plan: Scale Agent Workforce 30 → 54 in 6 Weeks

## Context

Today the Boldteq Software Factory runs **30 agents** across 6 departments. Three are critically overloaded (Koda, Quill, Rex), and three core capability blocks are missing: **stack-specific engineering depth** (3 stacks share one Koda), **deep design specialization** (only Vega + Pixel for all UI/UX), and **CRO mastery** (no agent owns conversion strategy).

The factory's mission requires bulk SaaS shipping across 3 stacks: **Next.js + Supabase + Railway**, **Shopify Native**, and **Shopify External**. Every project also needs **Resend transactional email** and **40%+ conversion** marketing/ecom pages — neither of which has a deep specialist today.

This plan locks in **24 net-new specialist agents** + **4 decompositions of overloaded agents**, executed in **6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents** under a strengthened HR team. Every new agent is narrow-by-design to maximize per-task token efficiency: each agent loads only the memory/skills it owns, never the full org's knowledge base.

**Boldteq B2B agency operations are deferred to v2** (post 5 paying clients on boldteq.com). All 24 new hires serve internal product velocity first.

**End-state:** 54 agents, every routing decision touches the most-specialized agent, token waste drops ~40%.

---

## Locked Decisions

| Total scale | 30 → 54 agents (24 net new + 4 decompositions) |
| Pace | 6 weekly cohorts of 5 agents/week + Week 0 prep |

| Design org | Bundle of 4: Ecom UI, Dashboard, Design System, Figma Synth (JSX→.fig) |

| Email org | 2 agents: Postmark (Resend infra) + Lifecycle (CRO email sequences) |
